_README: The address the HOST reads, per agent — not the one our installer picks.
§983/§985/§986. For two months Grok carried our hooks in
~/.grok/user-settings.json, a file it does not read: `grok inspect` showed
Hooks (0) there and Hooks (6) at the right address. Both instruments that produce a
compatibility table — the in-process test (compat_matrix.rs) and the published
bench (matrix-probe.mjs) — decided 'channel installed' by looking at what
the install had WRITTEN. This file is their shared source, because two
copies of the same table drift, and this journal already counts several.
paths: [] does NOT mean 'unknown'. It means 'the address is known and nothing live
is there' — the Qwen case. An agent ABSENT from this file is the unknown, and keeps the
Paths are relative to HOME, separated by /. Each entry says where its provenance was
READ: the host's binary or bundle, or its output.
`confirm` is the command that RE-PROVES the address by asking the host itself,
when it can answer. That is the form of proof Grok was missing for two
months: not « we wrote there », but « the host says it reads there ».

claude-code.why: Claude Code's documented settings file; it is also the one Grok and Codex scan for their Claude compatibility.

codex.why: The codex binary carries `hooks.json` in the same string table as `.codex`, `.claude` and `settings.local.json`.

droid.why: `persistHooksJson` writes <folderPath>/hooks.json, and `archiveLegacyHooksFile` renames the OLD <folderPath>/hooks/hooks.json to hooks.migrated.json.

copilot.why: app.js: the user hooks directory is OL(ea(void 0,'config'),'hooks'), scanned for *.json.

grok.why: `grok inspect` on a throwaway home: Hooks (0) from user-settings.json, Hooks (6) from ~/.grok/hooks/*.json (grok 1.0.0, 2026-09-11).

antigravity.why: Probed against the `agy` binary itself — see install_antigravity_cli_hooks.

aider.why: `aider --help`: '-c CONFIG_FILE … default: search for .aider.conf.yml in git root, cwd or home directory', and `--load LOAD_FILE` is the key we set there.

opencode.why: XDG plugin directory loaded by opencode — confirmed by the host: `opencode debug config` lists our file under the `plugin` key (2026-09-11).

pi.why: Its loader spells out its rules: « Direct files: `extensions/*.ts` or `*.js` → load », on `globalExtDir = path.join(getAgentDir(), "extensions")`, and `getAgentDir()` returns `homedir()/.pi/agent` (dist/core/extensions/loader.js + dist/config.js, 2026-09-11). Careful: `pi list` answers « No packages installed » even when the file is loaded — it lists the packages REGISTERED in the settings, not what the loader discovers.

qwen-code.why: `paths: []` here used to mean « live file, dead entries » (§982: our entries carried BeforeTool/AfterTool while the host speaks Claude Code's names). The entries are now written as PreToolUse / SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit — verified 2026-09-12 on a throwaway home — so the address is a channel again. Leaving it empty made qwen's hook INVISIBLE to the bench, which then fell back to the shared contract and published green what no agent channel carried.
qwen-code.confirm: tokenade install --only qwen-code  # then read hooks.PreToolUse in ~/.qwen/settings.json

kilo-code.why: `kilo debug paths` answers `config <XDG_CONFIG_HOME>/kilo`, and `kilo debug config` lists our file under the `plugin` key after an install into a throwaway home (2026-09-11).

_REGISTERED_BY_THE_HOST.why: openclaw and cline do not accept an address: we HAND them a directory and their CLI decides where the copy lives (cline writes one more hashed directory on every call). Their proof of delivery is therefore not a path but the host's answer, and it can be re-run.
_REGISTERED_BY_THE_HOST.openclaw: openclaw plugins list   # line « Tokenade … enabled … ~/.tokenade/openclaw-plugin/index.js » (verified 2026-09-11)
_REGISTERED_BY_THE_HOST.cline: after an install into a throwaway HOME, `<HOME>/.cline/plugins/_installed/local/cline-plugin-*/package/tokenade.ts` exists (verified 2026-09-11)

hermes.why: Proof by execution rather than by reading: the bridge writes `hook-registered` then `hook-fired` next to itself, and both were present and dated that day on this machine (2026-09-11).
hermes.confirm: ls -la ~/.hermes/plugins/tokenade/hook-fired   # the timestamp says when it last ran
